```typescript
const defaultSeedPassword = process.env.SEED_DEFAULT_PASSWORD;
```

```typescript
            address: p.address,
            status: 'active',

    Promise.all(
```

`lines.join('\n')` strips the trailing newline if the original file had one (since `split('\n')` on a file ending with `\n` produces an empty string as the last element, but `join('\n')` does not append a trailing newline). ### `scripts/i18n-coverage.ts` (2 issues)

**🐛 Bug** · lines 29-39

The `extractKeys` function does not recurse into arrays of objects, so nested keys inside arrays (e.g., `items[0].name`) are not extracted. If any translation file uses arrays of objects, those keys will be missing from the coverage analysis.

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```typescript
    function extractKeys(obj: unknown, prefix = '') {
      if (typeof obj !== 'object' || obj === null) return;
      if (Array.isArray(obj)) {
        for (let i = 0; i < obj.length; i++) {
          extractKeys(obj[i], prefix ? `${prefix}.${i}` : `${i}`);
        }
        return;
      }
      for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(obj as Record<string, unknown>)) {
        const fullKey = prefix ? `${prefix}.${key}` : key;
        if (typeof value === 'object' && value !== null) {
          extractKeys(value, fullKey);
        } else {
          keys.add(fullKey);
        }
      }
    }
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>:clipboard: Existing Code</summary>

```typescript
    function extractKeys(obj: unknown, prefix = '') {
      if (typeof obj !== 'object' || obj === null || Array.isArray(obj)) return;
      for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(obj as Record<string, unknown>)) {
        const fullKey = prefix ? `${prefix}.${key}` : key;
        if (typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value)) {
          extractKeys(value, fullKey);
        } else {
          keys.add(fullKey);
        }
      }
    }
```
</details>

### `scripts/test-dashboard.js`

**🔧 Maintainability** · lines 14-22

The 'http' module's callback-based API intermixes with setTimeout in a way that is error-prone. Consider using a modern HTTP client with native timeout support (e.g., node-fetch or undici) or the built-in fetch in Node.js 18+, which would eliminate the manual timeout and double-callback issues entirely.

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```javascript
// Using Node.js 18+ built-in fetch:
async function fetchPage(path) {
  const controller = new AbortController();
  setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 15000);
  const res = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:3000${path}`, { signal: controller.signal });
  const body = await res.text();
  return { statusCode: res.status, body };
}
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>:clipboard: Existing Code</summary>

```javascript
function fetchPage(path, cb) {
  const req = http.get(`http://127.0.0.1:3000${path}`, (res) => {
    let body = '';
    res.on('data', (chunk) => body += chunk);
    res.on('end', () => cb(null, res.statusCode, body));
  });
  req.on('error', (err) => cb(err));
  setTimeout(() => { req.destroy(); cb(new Error('timeout')); }, 15000);
}
```
</details>

```typescript
        where: {

            { senderId: { notIn: Array.from(userIds) } },
            { recipientId: { notIn: Array.from(userIds) } },
          ],
        },
      });
      if (orphanedMessages > 0) {
```

**🔧 Maintainability**

No print styles are defined despite the `export-btn` suggesting print/export workflows. When users attempt to print (Ctrl+P), the responsive breakpoint may trigger `min-width: 1200px` on table rows, causing horizontal overflow and cut-off in PDF output. Additionally, backgrounds (such as gradient on the button and header) will be stripped by browser defaults, and badges with `color` only may lose meaning. Consider a `@media print` block that removes unnecessary styles (shadows, backgrounds), forces full-width display, and ensures text remains visible.

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```
@media print {
  .audit-client {
    padding: 0;
  }

  .audit-client .export-btn {
    display: none;
  }

  .audit-client .panels-grid {
    grid-template-columns: 1fr;
  }

  .audit-table-card {
    box-shadow: none;
    border: 1px solid #ccc;
  }

  .audit-table-head,
  .audit-table-row {
    min-width: auto;
    page-break-inside: avoid;
  }

  .badge {
    border: 1px solid currentColor;
    background: none;
  }

  .badge::before {
    display: none;
  }
}
```
</details>

### `src/app/[locale]/admin/organizations/organizations.css` (3 issues)

**🐛 Bug** · lines 191-192

**Missing vendor prefix for `backdrop-filter`.** While `backdrop-filter` is well-supported in modern browsers, older Safari (pre-15.4) and early WebKit browsers require the `-webkit-backdrop-filter` prefix. Without it, the modal backdrop will render as a flat semi-transparent overlay in those browsers instead of the intended blurred glass effect.

Add the prefixed property before the standard one:
```css
-webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(4px);
backdrop-filter: blur(4px);
```

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```
  background: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.5);
  -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(4px);
  backdrop-filter: blur(4px);
```
</details>

**🔧 Maintainability** · lines 11-15

**CSS Grid without explicit `grid-template-columns`.** Both `.table-head` and `.table-row` use `display: grid` but do not define column templates. This means the column layout is entirely dependent on inline `grid-template-columns` styles injected by the JSX/TSX component. If the inline styles are missing, malformed, or the number of grid items doesn't match, the layout will collapse. Consider defining a default `grid-template-columns` as a fallback (e.g., using `auto-fit` or a sensible fixed ratio) so the table is robust even if the component fails to provide inline styles.

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```
.table-head {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(100px, 1fr));
  background: linear-gradient(180deg, #f8fafc, #f5f7fb);
  border-bottom: 1px solid #dfe7f1;
}
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>:clipboard: Existing Code</summary>

```

  display: grid;
  background: linear-gradient(180deg, #f8fafc, #f5f7fb);
  border-bottom: 1px solid #dfe7f1;
```

**⚡ Performance** · lines 31-36

**Broad `transition: 0.2s` on `.table-row`.** The transition property on `.table-row { transition: 0.2s; } without specifying which properties to animate means the browser will interpolate *all* animatable CSS properties on hover. While impact is minor for admin tables, explicitly scoping to the properties that actually change (`background-color`) is a best-practice optimization that avoids potential jank on large table datasets:
```css
transition: background-color 0.2s;
```

<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```
.table-row {
  display: grid;
  min-height: 68px;
  background: #fff;
  transition: background-color 0.2s;
}
```
</details>

### `src/app/api/admin/audit/route.ts`

**🐛 Bug** · lines 8-12

`parseDateParam` uses `new Date(s)` which is extremely lenient — it accepts many non-ISO formats (e.g., `'2024/07/29'`, `'July 29, 2024'`). An invalid-format date string that happens to parse will be silently accepted, potentially causing unexpected behavior in the audit service. Consider validating against a strict ISO 8601 format or using a dedicated date library.

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```typescript
function parseDateParam(s: string | null): string | undefined {
  if (!s) return undefined;
  // Validate strict ISO 8601 format
  const d = new Date(s);
  if (Number.isNaN(d.getTime()) || d.toISOString().slice(0, 10) !== s.slice(0, 10)) {
    return undefined;
  }
  return s;
}
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>:clipboard: Existing Code</summary>

```typescript
function parseDateParam(s: string | null): string | undefined {
  if (!s) return undefined;
  const d = new Date(s);
  return Number.isNaN(d.getTime()) ? undefined : s;
}
```
</details>

### `src/app/api/swagger/route.ts`

**🔧 Maintainability** · lines 315-321

The GET handler has no error handling. If `spec` contains circular references or `NextResponse.json` fails to serialize it, the route will return a 500 with no useful error context. Consider wrapping in try/catch.

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```typescript
export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
  try {
    return NextResponse.json(spec, {
      headers: {
        'Cache-Control': 'no-store',
      },
    });
  } catch (error) {
    return NextResponse.json(
      { error: 'Failed to generate Swagger specification' },
      { status: 500 }
    );
  }
}
```
</details>

<summary>:clipboard: Existing Code</summary>

```typescript
export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {

    },
  });
}
```

**🐛 Bug** · lines 17-19

`formatRelativeTime` does not guard against invalid date strings. Passing `undefined`, `null`, or a malformed date string to `new Date()` produces `Invalid Date`, whose `getTime()` returns `NaN`, causing all arithmetic to propagate `NaN` and `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` to return a nonsensical result like "NaN minutes ago". Add a guard: if `isNaN(date.getTime())`, return a fallback string (e.g., the raw `dateString` or a translated "unknown" label).

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```typescript
function formatRelativeTime(dateString: string): string {
  const date = new Date(dateString);
  if (isNaN(date.getTime())) {
    return dateString;
  }
  const now = new Date();
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>:clipboard: Existing Code</summary>

```typescript
function formatRelativeTime(dateString: string): string {
  const date = new Date(dateString);
  const now = new Date();
```
</details>

**🐛 Bug** · lines 50-51

**`parseInt` fallback swallows legitimate page `0`.** The expression `parseInt(pageParam, 10) || 1` converts `0` to `1` because `0` is falsy. While pages typically start at 1, if a URL ever contains `page=0`, it will silently be treated as page 1. Use `Number.isNaN` check instead: `parseInt(pageParam, 10)` is `NaN` for invalid input, so use `isNaN(parsed) ? 1 : parsed`.

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```typescript
    const parsedPage = pageParam ? parseInt(pageParam, 10) : 1;
    const newPage = isNaN(parsedPage) || parsedPage < 1 ? 1 : parsedPage;
    const parsedPageSize = pageSizeParam ? parseInt(pageSizeParam, 10) : 10;
    const newPageSize = isNaN(parsedPageSize) || parsedPageSize < 1 ? 10 : parsedPageSize;
```
</details>

<summary>:clipboard: Existing Code</summary>


### `src/components/admin/AdminVaultFilesTable.tsx` (4 issues)

**🔒 Security** · lines 232-237

**Potential security concern: unsanitized ID in URL path.**

The vault file ID is interpolated directly into the download URL without any encoding or validation. If the ID is not guaranteed to be a safe slug (e.g., UUID), a malicious or malformed ID containing path traversal characters (`../`, `..%2F`) could allow an attacker to craft a request to an unintended API endpoint.

Consider validating that `record.vaultFile.id` matches an expected format (e.g., UUID regex) before rendering the link, or encode it with `encodeURIComponent`.

<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```typescript
                  href={`/api/vault/${encodeURIComponent(record.vaultFile.id)}/download`}
                  className="vault-action-link"
                >

```

**🐛 Bug** · lines 26-33

**Edge case: filename ending with a dot produces empty extension string.**

For a filename like `"report."`:
- `split('.')` → `['report', '']`
- `.pop()` → `''`
- `''.toUpperCase()` → `''`
- `'' ?? 'FILE'` → `''` (empty string is not nullish, so the fallback is never used)

The file icon would render with an empty label, which looks broken.

Consider adding an explicit check: if `ext === ''` or `ext.length === 0`, fall back to `'FILE'`.

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```typescript
function getFileExt(filename: string | null): string {
  if (!filename) return 'FILE';
  const ext = filename.split('.').pop()?.toUpperCase() || 'FILE';
  if (['PDF', 'DOC', 'DOCX', 'XLS', 'XLSX', 'ZIP', 'RAR', 'PNG', 'JPG'].includes(ext)) {
    return ext.length > 3 ? ext.slice(0, 3) : ext;
  }
  return ext.slice(0, 3) || 'FILE';
}
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>:clipboard: Existing Code</summary>

```typescript
function getFileExt(filename: string | null): string {
  if (!filename) return 'FILE';
  const ext = filename.split('.').pop()?.toUpperCase() ?? 'FILE';
  if (['PDF', 'DOC', 'DOCX', 'XLS', 'XLSX', 'ZIP', 'RAR', 'PNG', 'JPG'].includes(ext)) {
    return ext.length > 3 ? ext.slice(0, 3) : ext;
  }
  return ext.slice(0, 3);
}
```
</details>

**🐛 Bug** · lines 26-33

**Misleading extension for dotfiles (e.g., `.gitignore`).**

For a filename like `".gitignore"`:
- `split('.')` → `['', 'gitignore']`
- `.pop()` → `'gitignore'`
- The function returns `'GIT'` (truncated to 3 chars), which is not a real extension.

Consider detecting the case where the filename starts with a dot (hidden file / no extension) and returning `'FILE'` instead.

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```typescript
function getFileExt(filename: string | null): string {
  if (!filename) return 'FILE';
  const parts = filename.split('.');
  if (parts.length === 1 || (parts.length === 2 && parts[0] === '')) return 'FILE';
  const ext = parts.pop()?.toUpperCase() || 'FILE';
  if (['PDF', 'DOC', 'DOCX', 'XLS', 'XLSX', 'ZIP', 'RAR', 'PNG', 'JPG'].includes(ext)) {
    return ext.length > 3 ? ext.slice(0, 3) : ext;
  }
  return ext.slice(0, 3) || 'FILE';
}
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>:clipboard: Existing Code</summary>

```typescript
function getFileExt(filename: string | null): string {

    return ext.length > 3 ? ext.slice(0, 3) : ext;
  }
  return ext.slice(0, 3);
```

**🐛 Bug** · lines 35-51

**PNG and JPG file types lack dedicated icon styles.**

`getFileExt` includes `'PNG'` and `'JPG'` in its recognized list, but `getFileIconStyle` does not have a corresponding `case` for them — they fall through to the `default` style. This is inconsistent: image files will display with the same default purple icon as any other unrecognized type, rather than a distinct image-appropriate style.

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```typescript

```

<details>
<summary>:clipboard: Existing Code</summary>

```typescript
function getFileIconStyle(ext: string): { bg: string; color: string } {
  switch (ext) {
    case 'PDF':
      return { bg: 'linear-gradient(135deg, #dbeafe, #eff6ff)', color: 'var(--color-info)' };
    case 'DOC':
    case 'DOCX':
      return { bg: 'linear-gradient(135deg, #dbeafe, #eff6ff)', color: '#1d4ed8' };
    case 'XLS':
    case 'XLSX':
      return { bg: 'linear-gradient(135deg, #d1fae5, #ecfdf5)', color: '#059669' };
    case 'ZIP':
    case 'RAR':
      return { bg: 'linear-gradient(135deg, #fef3c7, #fffbeb)', color: '#d97706' };
    default:
      return { bg: 'linear-gradient(135deg, #e0e7ff, #eef2ff)', color: '#4f46e5' };
  }
}
```
</details>

### `src/components/admin/ChatActivityPanel.tsx` (2 issues)

**🔧 Maintainability** · lines 247-260

`handleRetryLoad` uses `.then().catch()` chaining while the rest of the file consistently uses `async/await`. For consistency and readability, consider rewriting this as an `async` function with `try/catch`.

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```typescript
  const handleRetryLoad = useCallback(async () => {
    setIsLoading(true);
    setError(null);
    try {
      const res = await fetch(`/api/admin/requests/${requestId}/chat`);
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error('Failed to load chat history');
      const data = await res.json();
      if (!mountedRef.current) return;
      setMessages(data.messages ?? []);
    } catch (err) {
      if (!mountedRef.current) return;
      setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Unknown error');
    } finally {
      if (mountedRef.current) setIsLoading(false);
    }
  }, [requestId]);
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>:clipboard: Existing Code</summary>

```typescript
  const handleRetryLoad = useCallback(() => {
    setIsLoading(true);
    setError(null);
    fetch(`/api/admin/requests/${requestId}/chat`)
      .then((res) => res.json())
      .then((data) => {
        setMessages(data.messages ?? []);
        setIsLoading(false);
      })
      .catch((err) => {
        setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Unknown error');
        setIsLoading(false);
      });
  }, [requestId]);
```
</details>

### `src/components/admin/admin-requests-client.css` (2 issues)

**** · lines 144-161

Duplicate responsive breakpoint for `.stats-grid`: the file defines `@media (max-width: 1400px)` setting `grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr)` on lines ~120-124, and `@media (max-width: 1300px)` at lines ~702-705 redundantly setting `grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr)`. The 1300px breakpoint will take precedence when the viewport is below 1300px (including below 1400px), effectively making the 1400px breakpoint only apply between 1301px and 1400px. This layered approach works, but the 1400px breakpoint has a very narrow effective window. Consider consolidating into a single coherent breakpoint strategy to reduce confusion.

<details>
<summary>:clipboard: Existing Code</summary>

```
/* Responsive Stats Grid */
@media (max-width: 1400px) {
  .stats-grid {
    grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
  }
}

@media (max-width: 1024px) {
  .stats-grid {
    grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
  }
}

@media (max-width: 640px) {
  .stats-grid {
    grid-template-columns: 1fr;
  }
}
```
</details>

### `src/components/admin/admin.css` (2 issues)

**🐛 Bug** · lines 150-164

The .timeline::before pseudo-element uses percentage-based positioning (top: 8px, bottom: 8px) which depends on the parent .timeline having a defined height. If .timeline contains dynamically loaded content or varying numbers of items, and the parent's height isn't explicitly set, the ::before pseudo-element's height may collapse or stretch incorrectly — the vertical line may not span the full height of the timeline items. Consider using absolute values or ensuring the parent has a proper layout context.

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```
.timeline {
  position: relative;
  display: grid;
  gap: 18px;
}

.timeline::before {
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  left: 13px;
  top: 8px;
  bottom: 8px;
  width: 2px;
  background: #e2e8f0;
}
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>:clipboard: Existing Code</summary>

**Missing `text-overflow` companion properties on `.stackStrong` and `.stackSpan`.** These classes declare `white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;` for text truncation, but the parent element's grid context (e.g., `.workspaceCard` with `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) auto`) may not enforce `overflow: hidden` all the way up the chain, causing the ellipsis to fail. Adding `min-width: 0` to `.workspaceCard`, `.partnerCard`, `.docCard` ensures truncation works reliably.

```
  grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) auto;
  gap: 14px;
  align-items: center;
  min-width: 0;

}
```

### `src/components/create-request/WizardProvider.tsx` (3 issues)

**⚡ Performance** · lines 81-123

The `actions` object is recreated on every render, which means the context value `{ state, dispatch, actions }` changes every render, causing all `useWizard()` consumers to re-render even when only unrelated state changes. Consider wrapping `actions` in `useMemo` with an empty dependency array (since all individual action callbacks are already stable via `useCallback` with `[]` dependencies, except `nextStep`/`prevStep`).

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```typescript

    goToStep: (step: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5) => {
      dispatch({ type: 'SET_STEP', payload: step });
    },
    nextStep: () => {
      const next = Math.min(state.step + 1, 5) as 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5;
      dispatch({ type: 'SET_STEP', payload: next });
    },
    prevStep: () => {
      const prev = Math.max(state.step - 1, 1) as 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5;
      dispatch({ type: 'SET_STEP', payload: prev });
    },
    setDomain: (domainId: string) => {
      dispatch({ type: 'SET_DOMAIN', payload: domainId });
    },
    setService: (serviceType: string) => {
      dispatch({ type: 'SET_SERVICE', payload: serviceType });

    setAnswer: (key: string, value: string) => {
      dispatch({ type: 'SET_ANSWER', key, value });
    },
    addFile: (file: { vaultFileId: string; filename: string; size: number }) => {
      dispatch({ type: 'ADD_FILE', payload: file });
    },
    removeFile: (vaultFileId: string) => {
      dispatch({ type: 'REMOVE_FILE', payload: vaultFileId });
    },
    setPriority: (priority: 'normal' | 'urgent') => {
      dispatch({ type: 'SET_PRIORITY', payload: priority });

    setContact: (contact: Partial<WizardState['contactInfo']>) => {

    setDraftId: (draftId: string) => {
      dispatch({ type: 'SET_DRAFT_ID', payload: draftId });
    },
    setDirty: (dirty: boolean) => {
      dispatch({ type: 'SET_DIRTY', payload: dirty });
    },
    reset: () => {
      dispatch({ type: 'RESET' });
    },
  }), [state.step]);
```

### `src/components/dashboard/RecentDocuments.tsx` (2 issues)

**🐛 Bug** · lines 15-17

The `formatFileSize` function can produce an out-of-bounds array access for files ≥ 1TB (1024^4 bytes). The `sizes` array only goes up to index 3 ('GB'), but `Math.floor(Math.log(bytes) / Math.log(k))` would return 4 for TB-sized files, causing `sizes[4]` to be `undefined` and displaying e.g. '1.1 undefined'. Consider adding 'TB' to the array or clamping the index.

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```typescript
  const sizes = ['B', 'KB', 'MB', 'GB', 'TB'];
  const i = Math.min(Math.floor(Math.log(bytes) / Math.log(k)), sizes.length - 1);
  return parseFloat((bytes / Math.pow(k, i)).toFixed(1)) + ' ' + sizes[i];
```
</details>

```typescript
  const sizes = ['B', 'KB', 'MB', 'GB'];
  const i = Math.floor(Math.log(bytes) / Math.log(k));

```

**🐛 Bug** · line 61

**`toISOString()` can throw `RangeError` for dates with years outside 0–9999.**

If a valid `Date` object has a year < 0 or >= 10000 (e.g., `new Date('10000-01-01')`), `d.toISOString()` throws a `RangeError` which would crash the render. The `isNaN` guard on line 31 does not catch this because `d.getTime()` returns a valid number for such dates.

Consider wrapping `d.toISOString()` in a try/catch or using a fallback format for the `dateTime` attribute.

**🔒 Security** · lines 56-58

**`timezoneSuffix` is concatenated without validation.**

React's JSX escaping prevents XSS here, so this is not an injection vulnerability. Consider validating the suffix against an allowlist of known timezone labels, or generating it from a trusted timezone source rather than accepting free-form input.

```typescript
const MAX_FILE_SIZE = 50 * 1024 * 1024; // 50MB
const ALLOWED_TYPES = ['image/', 'application/pdf', 'text/'];

export async function uploadFile(
  file: File,
  options: {
    organizationId: string;
    requestId?: string;
    category?: string;
    visibility?: string;
  }
): Promise<FileUploadResponse> {
  if (file.size > MAX_FILE_SIZE) {
    throw new Error(`File size exceeds ${MAX_FILE_SIZE / 1024 / 1024}MB limit`);
  }
  if (!ALLOWED_TYPES.some(type => file.type.startsWith(type) || type.endsWith('/'))) {

  }

  const formData = new FormData();
```

```typescript
/**
 * Middleware factory for requiring a specific partner permission
 */
export function requirePartnerPermission(permission: PartnerPermission) {
  return async (req: NextRequest & { partnerContext?: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof getPartnerContext>> }) => {
    const context = await requirePartner({ required: true })(req);
    if (!context || context instanceof NextResponse) return context;

    if (!checkPermission((context as { role: PartnerRole }).role, permission)) {
      return NextResponse.json(
        { error: `Access denied. Required permission: ${permission}` },
        { status: 403 }
      );
    }

    req.partnerContext = context;
```
</details>

The function comment says getLinesArray 'splits numbered output back to raw lines array', but it does not actually strip the line number prefixes (e.g., '1| '). The function simply splits on '
', so the returned lines still contain the number prefix. Either the comment is misleading or the function is incomplete. Consider renaming or adding prefix-stripping logic.

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```typescript
/**
 * Split numbered output into raw lines array, stripping the line number prefix.
 */
export function getLinesArray(md: string): string[] {
  if (!md) return [];
  const normalized = md.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n').replace(/\r/g, '\n');
  return normalized.split('\n').map(line => line.replace(/^\d+\| /, ''));
}
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>:clipboard: Existing Code</summary>

```typescript
/**
 * Split numbered output back to raw lines array for position mapping.
 */

  if (!md) return [];
  return md.split('\n');
}
```
</details>

```typescript
  if (filters.matterTypeKey) and.push({ intakeSubmission: { is: { matterTypeKey: filters.matterTypeKey } } });
  if (filters.status) and.push({ status: filters.status });
  if (filters.assignedSpecialistId) and.push({ assignedSpecialistId: filters.assignedSpecialistId });
  if (filters.assignedReviewerId) and.push({ assignedReviewerId: filters.assignedReviewerId });
  if (filters.dateFrom || filters.dateTo) {
    and.push({ createdAt: { ...(filters.dateFrom ? { gte: filters.dateFrom } : {}), ...(filters.dateTo ? { lte: filters.dateTo } : {}) } });
  }
  if (filters.search && filters.search.length <= 200) {
    and.push({
      OR: [
        { title: { contains: filters.search } },
        { code: { contains: filters.search } },
      ],
    });
  }
  const where: Prisma.LegalRequestWhereInput = and.length ? { AND: and } : {};
```
</details>

### `src/lib/storage/commands/migrate.ts` (2 issues)

**🔧 Maintainability** · lines 56-68

**Low: Dynamic `import('fs')` inside async functions is unnecessary for a CLI script.**

This is a Node.js CLI tool, not a browser bundle. `fs` can be imported at the top of the file using a standard `import` statement. The dynamic imports add unnecessary complexity and make two separate `await import('fs')` calls that could be a single top-level import. Additionally, `readFileSync` and `writeFileSync` block the event loop in async functions; consider using the promise-based `fs/promises` API.

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```typescript
import { readFileSync, existsSync, writeFileSync } from 'fs';

async function loadMigrationLog(): Promise<MigrationLog> {
  try {
    if (!existsSync(MIGRATION_LOG_FILE)) {
      return { lastRun: new Date().toISOString(), completed: [], failed: [] };
    }
    const content = readFileSync(MIGRATION_LOG_FILE, 'utf-8');
    return JSON.parse(content);
  } catch {
    return { lastRun: new Date().toISOString(), completed: [], failed: [] };
  }
}
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>:clipboard: Existing Code</summary>

```typescript
async function loadMigrationLog(): Promise<MigrationLog> {
  try {
    const { readFileSync } = await import('fs');
    const { existsSync } = await import('fs');
    if (!existsSync(MIGRATION_LOG_FILE)) {
      return { lastRun: new Date().toISOString(), completed: [], failed: [] };
    }
    const content = readFileSync(MIGRATION_LOG_FILE, 'utf-8');
    return JSON.parse(content);
  } catch {
    return { lastRun: new Date().toISOString(), completed: [], failed: [] };
  }
}
```
</details>

### `src/lib/storage/utils/checksum.util.ts`

**🔒 Security** · line 10

MD5 is cryptographically broken and should not be used for any security-sensitive purpose. While `computeMd5` is correctly documented as being for "S3 ETag compatibility" (a legitimate non-security use case), the `ChecksumAlgorithm` type and the generic `computeChecksum` function accept `'md5'` without any deprecation warning or caveat in their JSDoc. This makes it easy for developers to inadvertently use MD5 in a security-sensitive context.

Consider adding a `@deprecated` note to the MD5 options, or restricting the `ChecksumAlgorithm` type to only secure algorithms while keeping `computeMd5` as a standalone escape hatch for S3 ETag compatibility.

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```typescript
export type ChecksumAlgorithm = 'sha256';
```
</details>

<summary>:clipboard: Existing Code</summary>

```typescript
}
```

The file defines both a `<table>`-based system (`.data-table`, `.data-table thead/th/td`) and a `<div>`-based CSS grid system (`.table-head`, `.table-row`, `.th`, `.td`).   font-size: var(--text-sm2);

```
  font-weight: 500;

}
```

### `src/styles/pages/admin/ai-assistant.css` (3 issues)

**🔧 Maintainability** · lines 367-384

Skeleton width modifiers (`.w-1-3`, `.w-full`, `.w-5-6`, `.w-2-3`) use a non-BEM naming convention that presumably comes from a utility framework (e.g., Tailwind). If the utility framework is not loaded, or if naming changes, these selectors silently fail and all skeleton lines will collapse to 0 width or become invisible. Consider defining widths inline with the component classes (e.g., `--skeleton-width` custom property) or using explicit BEM modifiers like `.ai-skeleton-text--full` to avoid external dependency.

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```
.ai-skeleton-text {
  height: 12px;
  border-radius: 3px;
  background: var(--color-border-soft);
  animation: ai-pulse 1.5s ease-in-out infinite;
}

.ai-skeleton-text--full  { width: 100%; }
.ai-skeleton-text--5-6th { width: 83%; }
.ai-skeleton-text--2-3rd { width: 66%; }

.ai-skeleton-line--1-3rd { width: 33%; }
```
</details>

Both `ai-spin` and `ai-pulse` animations use `opacity`/`transform` with no `will-change` or `contain` hints. The active annotation outline on line 73 hardcodes `#3b82f6` as a fallback for `var(--color-primary)`. If the design system's primary token changes (e.g., to indigo or teal), this fallback will be stale and the outline will silently be blue-500 instead of the intended theme color. **🎨 Style**

The font-family fallback chain `var(--font-sans, 'Inter', 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif)` places `system-ui` after named fonts. `system-ui` should typically come last in the fallback stack (after `sans-serif`), or it should be omitted entirely in favour of `sans-serif` as the ultimate fallback — the current ordering may cause the browser to skip `system-ui` and use `sans-serif` directly, though this is harmless in practice. Consider standardizing: `var(--font-sans, 'Inter', system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif)`.

`-webkit-line-clamp` usage here only has the `-webkit-box` display mode and `-webkit-box-orient: vertical`. If Firefox users see incorrect line clamping, consider using `line-clamp: 2` combined with `display: -webkit-box` for broader compatibility, or include the -moz- prefixed equivalents.

```
  line-height: 1.4;
  display: -webkit-box;
  display: -moz-box;
  -webkit-line-clamp: 2;
  line-clamp: 2;
  -webkit-box-orient: vertical;
  -moz-box-orient: vertical;
  overflow: hidden;
}
```

### `src/styles/pages/settings.css` (2 issues)

**🔧 Maintainability** · lines 426-446

The `.toggle::after` knob uses `transition: transform 0.2s` but the position change between on/off states is driven by swapping `right`/`left` properties, not `transform`. This means the knob will snap position (no animation) when toggling. For a smooth sliding effect, use `transform: translateX(...)` instead of swapping `right`/`left`. Example: default to `right: 3px` with `transform: translateX(0)`, and `.toggle.off::after` to `transform: translateX(-20px)`.

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```
.toggle::after {
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  right: 3px;
  top: 3px;
  width: 20px;
  height: 20px;
  background: var(--color-surface);
  border-radius: 50%;
  box-shadow: 0 1px 3px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.2);
  transition: transform 0.2s;
  transform: translateX(0);
}

.toggle.off {
  background: var(--color-border-strong);
}

.toggle.off::after {
  right: auto;
  left: 3px;
  transform: translateX(0);
}
```
</details>

**⚡ Performance** · lines 207-215

The `.dark` class repeats the legacy alias block identically to `:root`. Since CSS custom properties inherit, these aliases in `.dark` will override the `:root` values with identical computed values. While functionally harmless, this adds unnecessary bytes and increases CSS parse time. Consider omitting aliases from `.dark` — they will inherit from `:root` automatically.

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```
  /* Legacy aliases inherit from :root — only override if values change */
  --muted: var(--color-text-muted);
```
</details>

### `tests/e2e/helpers/auth.ts`

**⚡ Performance** · lines 53-60

**Performance: Sequential selector iteration with individual timeouts in `logout()`.**

Each `isVisible({ timeout: 500 })` call waits up to 500ms before moving to the next selector. In the worst case (7 selectors × 500ms = 3.5s), plus the `waitForURL` timeout, logout can take a long time. Since the selectors are mutually exclusive (only one will match in a given locale), consider using `page.locator(selectors.join(',')).first()` with a single `isVisible` timeout, or use `Promise.race` to parallelize the visibility checks.

<details>
<summary>:bulb: Suggestion</summary>

```typescript
    // Combine all selectors into a single locator; Playwright checks all concurrently
    const combinedSelector = selectors.join(', ');
    const element = page.locator(combinedSelector).first();
    if (await element.isVisible({ timeout: 3000 })) {
      await element.click();
      await page.waitForURL(/\/login/, { timeout: 5000 });
      return;
    }
```
</details>

<summary>:clipboard: Existing Code</summary>
